title: Asking Questions
description: The question words, the questions you will actually need, and how to ask for help when you get lost.

lessons.title: Question words
lessons.goal: Learn the eight words that open almost every question.
notes: Almost all of them start with k — ki, kaun, kitthe, kadon, kiun, kiven. That is your memory hook.
Unlike English, the question word usually stays where the answer would go, near the end of the sentence.

lessons.title: Questions you will actually use
lessons.goal: Ask what something is, who someone is, and where things are.
notes: ki at the start of a sentence turns a statement into a yes/no question: ki tusin panjabi bolde ho?
The same word ki also means "what" — position tells you which is meant.

items.pa: ਪੰਜਾਬੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਇਹਨੂੰ ਕੀ ਕਹਿੰਦੇ ਹਨ?
items.roman: panjabi vich ihnu ki kahinde han?
items.en: What is this called in Punjabi?

lessons.title: When you get lost
lessons.goal: Say you did not understand and ask someone to slow down.
notes: These are the highest-value phrases in the whole course. Learn them cold — they keep a conversation alive when you are out of your depth.
Adding ji to a command softens it into a polite request: haule bolo ji.

dialogue.speaker: Stranger
dialogue.en: ...and then we went to the village.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.pa: ਮਾਫ਼ ਕਰਨਾ, ਮੈਨੂੰ ਸਮਝ ਨਹੀਂ ਆਇਆ। ਹੌਲੀ ਬੋਲੋ ਜੀ।
dialogue.roman: maaf karna, mainu samajh nahin aaya. hauli bolo ji.
dialogue.en: Sorry, I didn't understand. Please speak slowly.

dialogue.speaker: Stranger
dialogue.pa: ਕੋਈ ਗੱਲ ਨਹੀਂ! ਤੁਸੀਂ ਪੰਜਾਬੀ ਸਿੱਖ ਰਹੇ ਹੋ?
dialogue.roman: koi gall nahin! tusin panjabi sikh rahe ho?
